about: Movement order of an Act 3 crowd character (lower-city civilians walking their splines / detours): target, last seen position, arrival radius, a path state and a stuck counter. Created and driven by esv::crowds::CharacterMovementSystem::Update from the MoveTo/Detour/Patrol request singletons. Saved: model game.crowds.v0.MoveToComponent (32 bytes, alignment 4); bg3.exe+0x25FB4C0 loads it back (two vec3 through a level-offset transform, then the rest).

evidence.says: EoCServer.dll+0xD8C530 CharacterMovementSystem::Update copies the request's position (+0..+0xB, request stride 0x14) to +0..+0xB; the distance from the character to +0..+8 is compared with the radius at +0x18; live world coordinates

Update copies the character's ls::TransformComponent translation (+0x10..+0x18) to +0xC..+0x14 and each frame compares the current position with it (epsilon 1.19e-7) to detect a character that does not move
Update copies request+0xC here; arrival when squared distance <= radius^2; increased by 0.05 when the character is stuck for 30 frames; live 0.5..3.3

CharacterMovementSystem::Update (EoCServer.dll+0xD8C530) passes &component+0x1C as the 'unsigned int *' of esv::BehaviourMachine::SetState(EBehaviourLayer, BehaviourState*, unsigned int*, bool) when it sets the BSMove state, tests it with BehaviourMachine::VerifyState(layer 0, id) each frame, and when the order ends clears the layer only if the current state's id (+0x10) equals it; zeroed on a new request and when stuck.
Update increments the byte at +0x20 while the position is unchanged and resets it at 30 (0x1E) or when the character moves; live 0

esv::crowds::CharacterMovementSystem::Update (EoCServer.dll+0xD8C530) copies MoveToComponent byte +0x21 into a fresh eoc::PathSettings (constructor EoCShared.dll+0x3324E0: +4 = 2, +8 = 0) at +4 with the variant index +8 set to 0 - the uint8_t alternative of PathSettings' Speed (Script Extender: std::variant<uint8_t, float> Speed) - before putting the BSMove behaviour state on the character. Live 1..4 here; same default 2 as esv::crowds::SpawnComponent::PathMovementSpeed (game name), and the patrol request's MovementSpeed is switched on 1..4 with the assert 'Invalid m_PathMovementSpeed enum %d'.
